title: Bram and the Cover
premise: Kestrel Vane, a private security contractor haunted by a botched protection detail that killed her client, is pulled back into the field when a voiceprint — her own, recorded years ago — unlocks a server in Lisbon containing plans for a staged industrial 'accident' that will kill hundreds. The attack is being orchestrated by Halcyon Cover, the very firm she now works for, and the only other person who knows is Bram Okafor, the disgraced analyst she once betrayed to save herself. As Kestrel and Bram race to expose the plot before the scheduled blackout, she must choose between loyalty to the employer keeping her employed and fed, and the truth that could finally let her sleep. In the end she burns her own cover to broadcast the evidence, saves most of the target site's night shift, and turns state's witness — trading her career, and Bram's freedom, for a conscience that finally rests.
about_author: Wren Vasquez spent eight years consulting for risk-assessment firms before walking away to write about the people inside them. She lives in coastal Oregon with two rescue dogs and an unhealthy knowledge of lock-picking.

chapters.title: The Hours Between
chapters.summary: Kestrel Vane works a routine overnight detail for Halcyon Cover, running on four hours of broken sleep since the incident that killed her client. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: exhaustion as identity — she has made vigilance a substitute for peace.

chapters.title: Voiceprint
chapters.summary: A dead client's encrypted server pings awake in Lisbon, unlocked by Kestrel's own archived voiceprint. Inside: schematics for a staged failure at the Meridian processing plant. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: dread — the past has been waiting for her.

chapters.title: Company Man
chapters.summary: Kestrel reports the anomaly to her handler, Dane Mercer, and watches him lie smoothly about it. She copies what she can before the server wipes itself. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: first crack of betrayal; loyalty begins to feel like a leash.

chapters.title: Bram
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: three years earlier, Kestrel testified against analyst Bram Okafor to protect her own contract after the incident. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: his bitterness and his stubborn belief that Kestrel was coerced, not corrupt.

chapters.title: Lisbon Calling
chapters.summary: Bram, now scraping by as a security auditor, receives an anonymous file — the same Meridian schematics — and recognizes Kestrel's fingerprints in the metadata. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: reluctant hope tangled with old resentment.

chapters.title: Night Shift
chapters.summary: Kestrel visits Meridian under pretext of a routine audit and meets shift supervisor Ada Reyes, whose crew would be inside during the planned 'accident.' POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: the abstract threat acquires faces; belonging to the company means betraying these people.

chapters.title: Two Liars, One Table
chapters.summary: Bram confronts Kestrel at a transit hotel. They trade accusations, then trade data, agreeing to a fragile alliance neither trusts. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: grudging partnership; truth-telling between two practiced liars.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Betrayals
chapters.summary: Digging into Halcyon's finances, they find payments routed through shell companies tied to Meridian's insurer — someone profits enormously from the disaster. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: cold clarity; this isn't negligence, it's arithmetic.

chapters.title: Mercer's Offer
chapters.summary: Dane Mercer quietly offers Kestrel a promotion and a transfer far from everything — if she stops asking questions. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: temptation; survival has always meant looking away.

chapters.title: Tail Lights
chapters.summary: Kestrel realizes she's being followed and runs a counter-surveillance route through the city, losing the tail but confirming Halcyon knows about Bram. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: What Ada Saw
chapters.summary: Ada Reyes reveals maintenance crews were ordered to falsify pressure-valve inspections — the exact failure point of the planned accident. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: working-class dignity versus institutional gaslighting.

chapters.title: Deadline Math
chapters.summary: Bram decodes the server timestamps: the attack is scheduled for the plant's annual shutdown drill, eleven days out, when every alarm will be assumed false. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: the clock becomes a character; panic disciplined into planning.

chapters.title: Old Wounds, New Leverage
chapters.summary: Halcyon blackmails Kestrel with the full record of the incident, threatening to pin it all on her unless she delivers Bram. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: rock bottom — the price of survival named aloud.

chapters.title: The Confession
chapters.summary: Kestrel tells Bram everything about the incident and her testimony, expecting him to walk. Instead he says he already knew. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: forgiveness offered without absolution; trust rebuilt on honesty rather than innocence.

chapters.title: Inside the Cover
chapters.summary: Using Mercer's promotion as cover, Kestrel infiltrates Halcyon's operations floor and photographs the operational order authorizing the drill-day 'test.' POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: the traitor's high — using their loyalty test against them.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: Mercer discovers the theft; Kestrel's credentials die mid-escape and she goes dark, rendezvousing with Bram and Ada at Ada's cousin's garage. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: liberation in ruin — she has nothing left to lose, which feels like freedom.

chapters.title: Eleven Hours
chapters.summary: With regulators stonewalled and media uninterested, the trio plans to trigger the plant's independent failsafe manually during the drill, forcing a real evacuation record. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: desperate ingenuity; ordinary people improvising against an institution.

chapters.title: Drill Day
chapters.summary: The operation begins: Ada pulls her crew off the floor, Bram reaches the failsafe room, and Kestrel walks back into Halcyon's command post wearing a wire. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: The Accident That Didn't Happen
chapters.summary: Halcyon triggers the sabotage early; Bram forces the failsafe, venting the line harmlessly while sirens clear the site. Mercer realizes Kestrel is broadcasting everything live. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: climax — chaos, sacrifice, and the sound of alarms meaning rescue instead of death.

chapters.title: Aftermath Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Federal agents arrest Mercer and two Halcyon directors; the evidence holds, but Kestrel must surrender herself as part of the deal. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: grief and relief braided together; justice costs what it costs.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Kestrel testifies, mirroring and redeeming her testimony against Bram three years ago; charges against her are reduced, Bram's record is cleared. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: closure without erasure — the past acknowledged, not forgiven away.

chapters.title: Sleep
chapters.summary: Months later, Kestrel visits the rebuilt Meridian floor where Ada's crew works, then drives the coast road alone. That night, for the first time since the incident, she sleeps through till morning. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: quiet resolution — belonging earned not through loyalty to power, but to truth.
